The Dominicans try to figure out who the Cathars are by interrogating everyone. If you disagree with church orthodoxy, they will figure it out and burn you at the stake. Western Europe is one of the least innovative places due to the Inquisition and the power of the Catholic Church. The little Ice Age begins, followed by the Great Famine, more wars, and the Black Death, which kills about a third of the European population. People think this is God's punishment because the Church is corrupt and stagnant.

Rome becomes the true center of the Catholic Church for some, while others believe Ammon is the true center, creating legitimacy problems. Individuals challenge the orthodoxy; for instance, John Wycliffe was not punished during his lifetime but was later declared a heretic and executed by burning at the stake. Jan Hus leads the Hussite Wars, which none succeed in ending. However, Martin Luther emerges and successfully challenges the Catholic Church, leading to Protestantism.

There is a case of someone's friend whose husband had severe cancer; they prayed to the Catholic Church and later the cancer disappeared, believing it a miracle. This can be explained by the placebo effect, where belief in medicine affects your perception and reality. Cancer could be seen as a loss of faith, with cells splitting because you stop believing in yourself.

Next class, we will discuss the rise of capitalism.
